headline: Gratitude literally rewires your brain for happiness
universal_truth: What we appreciate, appreciates—attention creates more of what we focus on
fun_facts: Writing three things you're grateful for daily can increase happiness by 25% in just three weeks
Grateful people have 10% fewer stress-related illnesses and report sleeping better
Brain scans show gratitude activates the same reward pathways as food and money
discussion_questions: What's something small you take for granted that many people don't have?
Who has helped you that you've never properly thanked?
How does gratitude change the way you see problems?

hook.script: What if I told you there's a free, side-effect-free intervention that improves sleep, boosts immunity, increases happiness, and strengthens relationships? It takes five minutes a day. It's called gratitude—and the science behind it is remarkable.

cliff.script: Gratitude isn't just a nice feeling—it physically changes your brain. Researchers have watched it happen in brain scans. But how does simply being thankful create measurable changes in brain structure?
cliff.prompt: How does gratitude change the brain?

options.text: It strengthens neural pathways for positive thinking
options.response: Exactly. What you practice grows stronger—gratitude trains your brain to notice good.
It does release dopamine and serotonin, but the effects go deeper...

fact1.title: The Three-Week Effect
fact1.script: Dr. Martin Seligman found that writing down three things you're grateful for each night increases happiness by 25%—and the effect lasts months after you stop. That's not a mood boost; that's rewiring. Your brain learns to scan for positives instead of threats.

fact2.title: Health Benefits
fact2.script: Grateful people aren't just happier—they're healthier. Studies show 10% fewer stress-related illnesses, lower blood pressure, and better sleep quality. Gratitude reduces cortisol, your stress hormone. Thankfulness is literally medicine.

fact3.title: Reward Pathways
fact3.script: Brain imaging shows gratitude activates the hypothalamus and ventral tegmental area—the same reward circuits triggered by food, money, and social connection. Your brain treats thankfulness as its own kind of wealth.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Gratitude isn't about pretending everything is fine. It's about training your attention. Problems don't disappear when you're grateful—but they share space with good things you might otherwise miss.

outro.script: That's Day 12. Tomorrow, we'll explore what courage really means—and why it's not the absence of fear. Until then, try this: write down three specific things you're grateful for tonight.

growTrack.title: Gratitude Journal - Three Good Things
growTrack.learning_objective: Begin a gratitude practice with lasting brain benefits
growTrack.activity: Before bed tonight, write down three specific things you're grateful for today—and why. Not just 'family' but 'the way my daughter laughed at dinner.' Specificity matters. Do this for one week and notice what changes.
